text:
Arsenal’s hopes of earning automatic progression to the Champions League quarter-finals were dashed by OL Lyonnes, as the French side continued their statement form in Europe.
Goals in either half from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay were the difference at Meadow Park and Lyonnes are top of the table and still yet to concede in the league phase with one game remaining.
It feels like Lyonnes are playing with a fire and intensity fueled by their loss to Barcelona in May’s Champions League final. They look a more formidable, coherent and hungry side, on a mission to end a four-year run without lifting the trophy they won eight times in a 12-year period between 2011 and 2022.
The visit of the eight-time European champions was always going to be challenging for the Gunners and based on current form getting a result would be even tougher. Last season’s runners-up had scored 20 goals without conceding in their first four Champions League matches prior to their trip to Borehamwood and they have scored 49 in their nine Première Ligue games.
The lack of competitiveness in the France top flight also means they were able to rotate heavily at the weekend between their two European games. Jonatan Giráldez made 11 changes for their 1-0 defeat of Saint-Malo on Saturday before returning to his first-choice lineup against the 2025 Champions League winners.
Arsenal were not afforded the luxury of an easy league match after their battling 1-1 draw against Barcelona last week, playing a critical and tricky game with London City Lionesses, which also ended 1-1. Renée Slegers made two changes to the team that hosted ambitious London City, with Ona Batlle having picked up a knock Taylor Hinds played at left-back and Kyra Cooney-Cross started ahead of Kim Little.
They had their backs against the wall at a bitterly cold Meadow Park, as Giráldez’s Galacticos controlled the game. The away team had almost 69% possession in the first half and amassed 12 shots to Arsenal’s one.
The surprise was that Lyonnes weren’t further ahead at the break, with Brand’s 24th-minute goal the difference, the full-back sweeping in Vicki Bècho’s ball in from the right.
Brand was back to haunt the Gunners, having scored in both legs of last season’s semi-final between the two teams, with the French side progressing to face Barcelona in the final with a 4-3 aggregate win.
Arsenal were better after the break, but Lyonnes soaked up a brief spell of Arsenal pressure, Marie-Antoinette Katoto the only player left forward as they banked back and crowded the box to give the home players few options.
They increased their margin and dampened the mood soon after, Tabitha Chawinga’s cross from the left was collected by Katoto and the France forward laid it off for Dumornay who took a touch before powering the ball into the roof of the net.
It was an emphatic and unstoppable finish from one of the best players in the world as a mist lowered over Meadow Park.
It was a testament to the relationship between the club and the fans that the crowd remained in full voice, they urged the players in red and white forward, the North Bank doing all it could to lift the spirits of their struggling side.
There were no more goals and Arsenal’s single shot on target was almost the last kick of the game as a controlled Lyonnes performance demonstrated the gulf in quality between the sides.
Arsenal need to quickly move on, with West Ham their last game before the international break. They had needed a win to have any serious chance of earning a place in top four, avoiding a quarter-final playoff place.
They now sit eighth and will face Inter in their final league phase match in December, with the Italian side needing a win against the north London team to keep any hopes of a playoff place alive. That will not be easy, but a seeded playoff place is in their hands, if they want it.
